scope: Owner-requested game-wide audit of which games are strongest and weakest at the current state, the choice of a strong game as the reference model, and a gold-star tool for development. Claude catalogued 60 child-facing games with hash-bound scores on a twelve-criterion rubric drawn from the design-language rules, added tools/gold_star.py (rank, compare against the reference, check that every new game file is catalogued, render, rebind) with tests, wired it into the study loop (study summary, report lines, a Raise lane in the roadmap, the INT-GOLD-STAR recipe), recorded a P0 blocker (MA-PLAY-005, Chapter 2 story careers cannot start) and a P1 soft-lock (MA-OPERA-013), and chose the Mermaid Pool (Day One) as the candidate reference. No game file changes in this commit.

lessons.lesson: Trusted probes that call internal functions stay green while the child's real route is broken: no probe launched a Chapter 2 story career through the real route (MA-PLAY-005), and most minigame probes start games that no longer have a route.
Agent reports cite lines without files and miscount; scores must bind to verified functions, and counts must be recomputed by script before they are recorded (19, not 18, unmapped story steps).

strengths_observed.evidence: The gold-star scores and reference patterns are bound to hashes of the exact functions they judged and go stale when that code changes (tools/gold_star.py anchor_hash, --check).
The Mermaid Pool awards progress only after Roshan's hand has worked at the real fixture (DayOneContactAction2D), which made it the reference model.
